methods.label: Add moving time and stopped time
methods.explanation:
The total elapsed time includes both travel and stops. At \(40\) miles per hour, traveling \(a\) miles takes \(a/40\) hours.

The \(n\) stops last \(m\) minutes each, so together they take \(mn\) minutes. Since there are \(60\) minutes in an hour, this is \(mn/60\) hours. Adding the two times gives
\[
\frac{a}{40}+\frac{mn}{60}
=\frac{3a+2mn}{120}.
\]
The trip takes \(\boxed{\frac{3a+2mn}{120}}\) hours, choice A.
methods.levelReason: The reasoning uses distance divided by speed, multiplication for repeated stops, and elementary time conversion.
